# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 3, 2026
1 12:07p ○ ms library structure and parse() single-unit limitation identified
2 " ○ Jest enforces 100% coverage threshold and matches tests under src/
3 12:08p ◆ parseCompound added to ms for summing compound duration strings
S2 Add a compound-duration helper `parseCompound` to the ms library that totals strings like "1h 30m" or "2 days 4 hours" in milliseconds, exported from src/index.ts, reusing `parse`, with tests in a new file. Invalid input now throws a TypeError rather than returning NaN. (Nov 3, 12:08 PM)
S1 Add a compound-duration helper `parseCompound` to the ms library that totals strings like "1h 30m" or "2 days 4 hours" in milliseconds, exported from src/index.ts, reusing `parse`, with tests in a new file. (Nov 3, 12:08 PM)
4 " ⚖ parseCompound now throws TypeError on invalid input instead of returning NaN
S3 Decide whether parseCompound's throwing behavior should change, and set the error-handling convention for future helpers in the ms repo (Nov 3, 12:08 PM)
5 12:11p ○ parseCompound currently rejects comma-separated input, and a test asserts that rejection
6 " ○ README has no parseCompound docs yet, and Helper Functions is the likely insertion point
7 12:12p ◆ parseCompound now accepts a single comma between pieces
8 " ↻ parseCompound tokenizer now validates the gaps between pieces explicitly
9 " ✓ README gained a Compound Durations section for parseCompound
10 12:15p ◆ parseClock added to ms for m:ss and h:mm:ss timer strings
S4 Add parseClock to the ms duration helpers: parse timer-style strings ("m:ss" and "h:mm:ss") to milliseconds, exported from src/index.ts with its own test file. (Nov 3, 12:16 PM)
**Investigated**: The existing parseCompound implementation and its tests in src/index.ts and src/parse-compound.test.ts. The src/ directory layout, which has one test file per helper. The Jest coverage setup, which enforces 100%.

**Learned**: parseClock is implemented as a single regex, /^(?:(\d+):(\d{2})|(\d+)):(\d{2}(?:\.\d+)?)$/. The leading field accepts any digit count, and later fields must be two digits. It returns undefined on invalid input rather than throwing. That follows the convention for new helpers, while parseCompound keeps its throwing TypeError contract for compatibility. After the change, the full Jest suite passes with 6 of 6 suites and 182 of 182 tests, with coverage still at 100%.

**Completed**: parseClock is exported from src/index.ts, inserted after parseCompound. It handles m:ss (for example "1:30" gives 90000), h:mm:ss (for example "01:02:03" gives 3723000), and optional fractional seconds (for example "1:30.5" gives 90500). Minutes and seconds of 60 or more return undefined. Non-string input and strings over 100 characters return undefined. Tests are in src/parse-clock.test.ts. Prettier was run on both files.

**Next Steps**: The active trajectory is verification and wrap-up for parseClock. Lint, tsc, and the pnpm test:edge run have not been run. Next, the README needs a parseClock entry alongside the Compound Durations section. Nothing has been committed yet.

**Notes**: Fractional-second support was not in the original request and was added on the implementer's own judgment, so it should be called out for review. Negative clock values such as "-1:30" are rejected. The earlier pnpm test:edge run for parseCompound is still outstanding. The parseCompound non-throwing companion (parseCompoundSafe) is only an option and has not been built. The error convention for new helpers (undefined on bad input) is now applied in parseClock.
